items.title: Find cheaper platforms for your funds
items.headline: The fund rotation plan now shows when the same fund costs less at SAVR, with the yearly saving in kronor, and skips savings under 300 kronor.
items.summary: Add a same-fund venue lookup to fund_rotation
added: The rotation plan checks whether a cheaper venue offers the same fund. For every fee-bearing fund holding not held at SAVR, the plan looks up SAVR's published net fee for the same ISIN and currency. When that fee is below the booked fee, the holding is listed with its SEK/yr saving, ranked by saving, separately from the candidates that replace the fund.

Matches are exact. A holding matches only on identical ISIN and the share-class currency SAVR lists that ISIN under (the holdings file books values in SEK and does not carry the class currency, so SEK, USD and EUR are looked up; an ISIN is one share class, so a hit is the class held). Names are never matched. A fund SAVR does not list is counted as not listed; a holding whose fee is missing or an unverified placeholder is not a candidate and is counted as unchecked.

Small savings do not clutter the plan. When the lookup succeeded and the total same-fund saving is below 300 SEK/yr, the plan shows one summary line with the total instead of the section; candidates are still audited.
Every candidate is audited. Each venue-switch candidate is written to the rotation audit log with the booked fee, SAVR's fee, the position value and the saving.

items.title: Missing or unfinished daily prices get fixed
items.headline: Daily price data that is still preliminary or missing after a trading day is now re-fetched automatically, so charts and signals rest on final prices.
items.summary: After the pulse's existing intraday settle, run a straggler sweep over the active tickers
added: Every pulse re-fetches daily bars that are still unsettled after the intraday settle. An active ticker with any daily bar still provisional more than 2 hours after its session closed (a later in-progress bar does not hide it) has its daily rows re-fetched in the same pulse. When the provider has still not published a priced row, the bar stays provisional.

A closed session with no daily row is treated as a gap and re-requested. For each active ticker, every exchange trading day between its last settled daily bar and the last closed session that has no row is re-requested. Exchange holidays are not gaps.
The sweep is reported. Each pulse records the number of stragglers, each one's oldest unsettled session and why it is unsettled (provisional or missing), and how many were settled.
Bars coverage keeps counting only settled bars. The sweep does not change how coverage is measured.

items.title: Test several caution rules together, fairly
items.headline: New rules that cap or lower confidence in recommendations are now tested as one group against past results, with extra care so lucky outcomes aren't mistaken for real findings.
items.summary: One harness, scripts/evaluate_conviction_rule_batch.py, read-only
added: Candidate conviction rules are tested together, with multiple-testing correction. Proposed rules that gate, cap or demote conviction bands are evaluated as one pre-registered batch against the matured, ticker-clustered decision cohort. Each rule's verdict accounts for every other rule in the same batch (Holm correction at α = 0.05).

Each rule reports its power. A verdict states each arm's row count, distinct-ticker count and cohort count. A rule whose arm falls below its floor (10 distinct tickers by default, or the higher floor the rule pre-registered) is reported as underpowered, not as passed or killed.

Rules use point-in-time inputs only. A rule is admitted only if every input it reads was available before the decision date. A rule keyed on a scheduled event (an interim report date) may use the event's actual date as a stand-in for the publicly announced schedule, and states that assumption. Candidates that cannot be written as a per-call filter are listed as not admitted, with the reason, in every batch run's output.
The harness must reproduce past verdicts. Before a batch counts, the harness reproduces the recorded verdicts of earlier single-rule kill tests on the same cohort.

items.title: New test signal: crowding of small shareholders
items.headline: A trial signal now scores stocks lower when many private investors own them, running in the background without affecting recommendations until it proves itself.
items.summary: Register retail_crowding as a shadow decision component (±150, effective contribution zero) on the universe stock surface, under the existing shadow contract (data/policies/shadow_registry.yaml entry with a graduate_by deadline)
added: The owner-count leg of attention_flow SHALL NOT be re-submitted to the category gate with a positive sign. Spike S09 found the positive-sign owner construct fails (three gate failures), while the cross-sectional level with a negative sign carries the measured edge.

A shadow decision component retail_crowding (raw budget ±150, effective contribution zero) SHALL score each universe stock by the negative of its retail owner count, cross-sectionally z-scored over the names scored at the same as-of date and clipped to ±3. The owner count is read point-in-time from silver owners (basis == settled_weekly) on or before the as-of date and at most 28 days older than it. A name with no such reading, or a batch with fewer than 20 names holding one, returns insufficient_data:retail_crowding.
retail_crowding SHALL log −log(owner count / market cap) as an audit-only side output. The side output is never scored.

retail_crowding SHALL carry a shadow-registry entry with a graduate_by deadline. Its graduation evidence SHALL be restricted to steps on or after 2024-01-01, because the S09 spike measured the edge decaying after 2023.

items.title: Health check restructured, results unchanged
items.headline: The app's health check was reorganised so future checks are easier to add. A comparison test confirms it reports exactly the same results as before.
items.summary: Target shape: a new subpackage src/investor/audit_log/health/ (under the existing capability package, so no new top-level module), with product_health.py reduced to a re-export facade plus main.
added: The health snapshot SHALL be produced by a collector that reads as an ordered list of named metric sections: load the inputs once, then concatenate the output of each registered section builder.
Path configuration, the metric model, input loading, each metric family's readers and builders, trend-file persistence, and snapshot presentation SHALL each live in their own module.

Adding a health metric SHALL require editing only its family's readers and the section builder that owns its rows, or, for a new section, adding one builder and one entry in the ordered section registry — never the collector function itself.

Invariant: for identical repository state, the restructured collector SHALL produce the same metrics — names, target ids, order, values, details, numeric readings and statuses — and the same trend-file row and rendered snapshot as the pre-refactor collector, as proven by a golden equivalence test on fixed inputs that exists before the first structural change.

items.summary: For each item, the engineer decides whether the code or the spec is wrong, then either fixes the code (with a test) or amends the spec with a delta that records the decision
added: Every source named in the fundamentals source TTL, confidence and accepted-source tables SHALL be a source the fetcher actually calls; a listed source with no fetch path is a defect.
No fundamentals CLI argument or help text SHALL refer to the retired Interactive Brokers source. The fetch --isin argument is accepted for CLI compatibility and ignored.

items.title: More accurate valuation ratios across currencies
items.headline: Valuation ratios for companies reporting in one currency and trading in another are now corrected, leaving only a few percent of error instead of roughly elevenfold distortions. Short-interest figures also use a consistent basis.
items.summary: A shared investor.core.currency.repair_mixed_ratio divides such a ratio by the statement-to-quote rate (rough fixed rates; a few percent of error instead of 11x)
added: A company in the reference data MAY carry its Finansinspektionen issuer LEI. The ranking SHALL score such a company's short interest and short trend from the register by that LEI when the screening universe does not cover it, so Swedish names outside the universe (Hacksaw, Evolution, Kambi, Better Collective, Catena Media) carry the same short-interest sentiment as foreign peers instead of an empty category.

Short interest from the market-data provider SHALL be expressed as a share of shares outstanding, the Finansinspektionen register's basis, falling back to share of float only when the outstanding-basis figure is missing. Share of float runs several times higher for closely held companies (LVS 14.4% of float, 2.8% of shares outstanding), so mixing bases put foreign names over the 5%/10% sentiment thresholds that the same position in a Swedish name would not reach.

The register store SHALL answer the latest short ratio and the trailing trend direction for an issuer identified by its LEI, so listings outside the screening universe (stored without a resolved ticker) can be scored.

items.title: Large shareholding changes now tracked
items.headline: The app now collects Finansinspektionen's notices of big owners crossing ownership thresholds, showing who bought or sold, how much, and what type of holder they are.
items.summary: Add a fi-flagging-register capability under src/investor/short_positions/, mirroring the insider scraper: walk FI's börsinformation notification pages (finanscentralen.fi.se/search/EditFlagging.aspx?id=<n>, sequential ids
added: Major-shareholding notifications (flaggningar under LHFI 4 kap.) are sourced from Finansinspektionen's börsinformation database (finanscentralen.fi.se), one notification page per sequential notice id. The register is walked by id: an unknown id is a miss, a run of consecutive misses ends a forward walk, and a network error ends the walk while keeping the notices already read. Requests use the insider register's browser-compatible headers and a per-request pause.
Every fetched page is captured to bronze under source fi_flagging_register before parsing; the source counts as a wired provider pull in the bronze-capture health share.

Each notification is parsed into one event carrying: notice id, issuer, instrument and its ISIN when printed, holder name, holder type, FI's stated reason, direction (up, down or unchanged, from the share count before and after, else from the reason), the share and vote thresholds crossed, share and vote counts before, share count and percentages of shares, votes and shares-plus-instruments after, the transaction date and FI's publication timestamp. A page that prints FI's 0001-01-01 placeholder has no publication timestamp. The notice's contact person, and any identifier printed next to a natural person's name, are not stored. A page missing a required label is not parsed; the fetch logs PROVIDER CONTRACT BROKEN at ERROR so the healer journal scan surfaces it.

Holder type is assigned from a team-maintained name-to-type map in data/flagging_holder_types.yaml (passive, active_fund, industrial, investment_company, founder_insider, private_equity, activist, nominee, other); a holder absent from the map is typed unknown and the event is stored, never dropped. Name matching is case-insensitive and ignores legal-form suffixes and non-breaking spaces.

added: Company earnings curves - Every listed company in the reference file gets an earnings curve: revenue, operating income, EBITDA and net income per quarter. - Annual figures are used when the provider has no quarterly statement. items.title: Smarter market position score for gambling stocks
items.headline: A company's market position now reflects whether it is gaining or losing share in the regions where it actually earns its revenue.
items.summary: Market position (±200) averaged table ranks and measured share changes with equal weight, wherever they came from
added: Market position (±200) measures whether a company is gaining or losing ground in the markets where it earns its revenue. It replaces the earlier unweighted mean of table ranks and share changes.

Evidence is grouped by region. Within a region, the value is a weighted mean of: - Measured share momentum, at full weight. Per feed, half is the 12-month share change (full at ±5pp) and half is the change over the last three months (full at ±2pp). A feed whose latest month is more than three months old is skipped. When a jurisdiction's combined feed names the company, the state feeds of that vertical are left out so nothing is counted twice. - Static rank from a hand-entered share table, at half weight: 1.0 for rank 1, 0.5 for ranks 2–3, 0 below that. A table counts fully up to 180 days old, fades to nothing at 540 days, and an undated table never counts.

The score is the sum of the region values, each weighted by the company's revenue share in that region; weights summing above 1 are normalised. Revenue in regions without evidence counts as neutral. A company without a revenue mix weights each region at 0.25.

Re-evaluation over time: - The weights follow the revenue mix as it is refreshed from company reports. - Measured momentum follows each monthly feed. - Stale feeds and aged tables drop out on their own.

items.title: Gambling ranking gets four new scoring factors
items.headline: The gambling ranking now scores price momentum, profit margin, valuation and debt against comparable gambling companies, replacing the old value-investing category.
items.summary: Drop graham from the gambling composite and spend its 1000 points on four categories scored against the other gambling companies
added: The gambling composite leaves out the engine's graham category. The engine part of each row is the engine composite without graham, and graham is not shown among the ranking's categories.

Four categories replace graham's 1000 points. They are counted in the gambling part of the composite and scored against the other gambling companies ranked that day. Each is absent, never zero, when its input is missing: - 12-1 month price momentum (±300): the price return over twelve months, leaving out the most recent month, as a percentile across all ranked gambling companies. - Operating margin vs peers (±250): a percentile within the company's peer group. - EV/EBITDA vs peers (±250): cheaper scores higher, as a percentile within the peer group. A negative multiple counts as missing. - Leverage (0 to −200): a penalty only. Net debt / EBITDA at or below 1x costs nothing, and the full penalty applies at 5x or more.

A peer group is the business model, with land-based casinos split into Asia-Pacific and the rest. When fewer than four group members have a value, the company is scored against every ranked company with one.

items.title: Track record for gambling growth estimates
items.headline: Daily growth estimates are saved and compared with what companies actually report, so you can see how accurate they have been.
items.summary: Spike S18 could not show that regulator-measured growth leads the earnings reaction
added: Each day's quarter-to-date nowcast per company is recorded and never revised afterwards. Re-running a day replaces that day's rows only.

After a company reports, the quarter is resolved against its reported revenue growth. The nowcast used is the last one recorded strictly before the report date. The Nowcast tab shows the resolved quarters with their summary accuracy, and how each company's nowcast moved during the current quarter.

added: Market-level gambling revenue is collected from regulators that publish it: Ontario, Denmark and Spain monthly, Sweden quarterly. It is stored by jurisdiction, vertical and period in local currency, and refreshed on the feed cadence. A failing feed never stops the others.

When a jurisdiction has measured online revenue covering the latest twelve months, or four quarters, and the period before, its growth is the measured trailing growth. Otherwise it keeps the reference growth. Every jurisdiction states its growth basis, period, source and scope. items.headline: The ranking now uses each operator's monthly revenue in US states, published weeks before the company reports its quarter.
items.summary: Regulated US states publish each operator's monthly gaming revenue weeks before the listed companies report their quarter
added: The ranking has a fifth sector category, regulated GGR momentum (±400). It measures a company's gaming revenue growth in regulated markets that publish per-operator monthly figures. Each feed compares its own latest three months for the company with the same months a year earlier. Feeds are summed where all six months exist. A feed more than three months behind the newest data is left out.

The score reaches the full budget at ±30% growth and is weighted by how much of the company the measured markets cover: annualised measured revenue ÷ company revenue, with full weight at 20%. A measured footprint under one million dollars in three months gives no score.
Each ranking row reports the growth, acceleration, weight, measured revenue, feeds used and latest month behind the score.

Per-operator monthly figures are collected from the Indiana, Maryland, Massachusetts, Ohio, Iowa and Pennsylvania regulators in addition to New York, Connecticut and New Jersey. File locations are found from the regulators' listing pages, not assumed.

items.title: Daily ranking of listed gambling stocks
items.headline: Every listed gambling company now gets a daily score combining general signals with gambling-specific factors, so you can see which stocks look best.
items.summary: The Gambling sector page describes markets, regulation and companies, but it does not say which listed gambling stocks look best
added: Every listed company in the reference file is scored daily on the decision engine's signed-points scale (±10000). The composite is the engine's composite categories plus four gambling-sector categories, and each row reports the engine part and the sector part separately.
Engine categories come from the same batch scorer the daily pipeline uses, without the LLM panel, podcast and surge enrichments.

Sector categories, each signed and bounded by its budget, with no data reported as absent, never as zero: - Regulated revenue (±300), centred on 50% of revenue from licensed markets. The reported share is used when the reference file has one. Land-based and lottery companies count as fully licensed. Otherwise the share is the revenue mix weighted by each region's share of licensed online markets, and only when those regions cover at least half of the mix. Each row states which of the three bases it used. - Market growth (±200): growth of the company's markets weighted by its revenue mix, at full budget at ±15%. - Market position (±200): the mean of the company's standing across the market-share tables that name it and its measured share change against a year earlier. - Catalyst balance (±150): the net sign of regulatory catalysts in the company's markets from 90 days back to 180 days ahead, weighted by its revenue in each region. No catalyst is neutral.
Companies are ranked by composite with a deterministic tie-break. A company that cannot be fetched or fails the data-quality gate is listed as unscored with its reason.

items.title: Gambling stocks compared region by region
items.headline: You can now see which gambling companies lead each world region by revenue earned there, plus a combined whole-market view for US states and a Brazil ban adjustment.
items.summary: The owner reads the gambling sector by region — "the US is one market, Latin America one" — but the page answered "who leads" only state by state for the US (NY, CT) and not at all elsewhere: every non-US share table was empty because no regulator outside the US publishes operator revenue
added: Each world region is treated as one market. Its leaders are the listed and private or state-owned companies ranked by revenue earned in that region: latest annual revenue times the company's reported share of revenue from the region. Only revenue- or GGR-basis figures rank; stakes- or sales-basis figures are not mixed in. A company marked as a listed subsidiary of another tracked company is left out of the ranking so its revenue is not counted twice.
Operators above a size floor that publish no regional split are listed separately as global operators, so a region's ranking is read with them in mind.
A market whose model is prohibited keeps its last (pre-ban) GGR on its own row but is left out of regional and global online GGR totals.

For a jurisdiction with measured feeds from two or more states, the measured shares are also combined into one whole-market reading per vertical: operators are matched by brand across states and feeds and summed in dollars over the months every state has reported, with the states named and coverage stated against the jurisdiction's whole-market online GGR for that vertical. Handle share and hold appear only when every state reports handle. The combined table leads the jurisdiction's share tables.

items.title: Past delisted stocks now included in history
items.headline: Price and key-figure history now includes companies that left Stockholm exchanges since 2017, so backtests no longer flatter results by ignoring failures, with coverage gaps clearly flagged.
items.summary: Two legs, in order.
added: The silver lake holds prices and key figures for instruments that delisted from Nasdaq Stockholm or First North between 2017-01-01 and 2026-09-07, each marked delisted with its delisting date and source.
Every delisted instrument's rows carry the source that supplied them, so a reader can tell a backfilled name from a live one.
The coverage report states, per year, the number of delisted names found against the number of decided equity delistings in the source, and the share of the yearly cross-section they make up.
Where no source covers a year, the coverage report marks that year as unmeasured instead of reporting zero delistings.

items.title: Testing a paid source for delisted prices
items.headline: A capped, pre-defined trial will check whether a paid data provider can supply complete, accurate price history for stocks that have left the exchange.
items.summary: A bounded, pre-registered trial of one or both routes on a fixed sample of delisted Stockholm names, scored against the acceptance rule below
added: A paid price source SHALL be trialled only under an owner-approved spend cap recorded in the change's design note before the first paid request, and SHALL NOT be purchased by the trial itself.
The acceptance rule for a trial SHALL be written before any paid request, on a fixed sample of decided delistings with recorded delisting dates.

A delisted instrument SHALL pass the trial only when the source returns end-of-day bars from its first to its last tradable session with at least 95% of those sessions present, and its last bar falls within 5 trading days of its recorded delisting date.
Where a sampled instrument also has an overlapping window in another price source, closes SHALL agree within 0.5% on at least 98% of overlapping sessions.

items.title: Delisted companies now caught automatically
items.headline: Daily exchange notices are read to spot companies being removed from trading, so they drop out of your stock universe without manual upkeep.
items.summary: A delisted name only leaves the universe when someone adds it to data/exclusions.yaml by hand
added: Every day the system reads the captured Nasdaq exchange notices and recognises decided delistings of an issuer's shares: an exchange approval of a delisting application, a delisting notice naming the company, or an announced last day of trading in the shares.
Applications, board proposals, and notices about bonds, paid subscription shares, rights, warrants, treasury-share cancellations or other non-share instruments are not delistings.
A recognised delisting is matched to universe names by normalised company name, exactly; every share class of the issuer matches.
Each match is recorded once in a machine-written delistings file with the notice date, notice id, headline and link. Recorded entries are never removed by the system; reinstatement is a manual edit.

items.title: Börsdata data now collected and stored
items.headline: A new connection to the Börsdata financial data provider saves its full raw data daily, kept safely and within the provider's usage limits.
items.summary: A Börsdata client inside the data-lake source package that
added: The lake SHALL capture every GET operation of the Börsdata REST API that the subscription can reach into bronze, under borsdata_* source names separate from the borsapi_* (BörsAPI) sources, each capture stored raw, dated and immutable under the existing bronze rules.
The Börsdata client SHALL read its key from the owner's local credentials file and SHALL NOT store the key in the repo, a manifest line, a bronze payload, a log line or an error message.

The client SHALL keep every request within the vendor's rate limit, back off on a rate-limit response for the period the vendor gives, and record each day's call count against the vendor's daily guidance.

Per-instrument errors returned inside an array response (not found, not active, bad input, no global access) SHALL be captured as data with the instrument id, never dropped and never treated as a failed run.

items.title: Börsdata figures organised by when they were known
items.headline: Börsdata's prices, reports, insider trades and calendars are cleaned up so each figure only appears from the date it was truly available, avoiding hindsight.
items.summary: Silver tables built from the borsdata_* bronze captures, each with a declared availability rule, a vintage record where values can change, and an instrument id resolved through the instrument master by ISIN, with Börsdata's own instrument i
added: Silver SHALL hold Börsdata-derived tables for instruments, prices, splits, annual, quarterly and rolling-twelve-month reports, KPI history, screener snapshots, insider transactions, short positions, buybacks, the report calendar and the dividend calendar, each keyed by instrument id and a time column, and read through the as-of contract.
Each Börsdata silver table SHALL declare its availability rule in the lake's table catalogue. A consumer SHALL read availability from that rule only.
Where a value has no documented publication date, its availability SHALL be the first Börsdata capture that contained it, never an earlier date implied by its period.

A report row's availability SHALL be the vendor's report date only when the trial battery and the vendor validation have confirmed that field's meaning; until then it SHALL be the first capture that contained the row.

items.title: Börsdata checked against filings and prices
items.headline: Börsdata's numbers must pass accuracy tests against company filings and independent prices, using thresholds fixed beforehand, before any score relies on them.
items.summary: A validation gate that compares Börsdata against those four references, with thresholds written down before the first run and a verdict file that records every miss by class
added: The lake SHALL validate Börsdata data against independent references before any Börsdata-derived table is read by a score, replay or health metric: ESEF annual statements, MFN report key figures, the BörsAPI cross-check captures, yfinance daily bars and the MFN release timestamps.
The validation thresholds SHALL be those written in the change's spec before any Börsdata comparison is run, and SHALL NOT be changed after a result is seen; a change requires a new proposal.
Key-figure agreement SHALL use the same relative tolerance and pass share as the ESEF accuracy gate, and SHALL exclude currency-mismatched and about-1000×-scale-mismatched pairs from eligibility.
Price agreement SHALL pass when at least 98% of overlapping sessions in windows with no corporate action agree with the reference within 0.5%.

items.title: Historical replays can use Börsdata figures
items.headline: Past-period replays of the strategy can now draw on Börsdata fundamentals as they were known on each date, without peeking ahead.
items.summary: A replay history provider that reads Börsdata silver (from borsdata-silver-point-in-time) through the as-of contract, and feeds the existing replay input slots for non-technical categories
added: A replay policy that opts in SHALL receive Börsdata-derived fundamentals, KPI and price inputs for each step, read only from Börsdata silver through the as-of contract, so each input is the one visible on the step's decision date.
A policy that does not opt in SHALL replay exactly as it replays without this provider, with identical composite, action and trades.
An input whose Börsdata availability is unknown or absent SHALL stay absent for that step, never zero and never back-filled from a later value.

A replayed input that the live path also computes from its own sources SHALL be computed under one shared definition for both paths, and a parity test SHALL show agreement inside the replay's existing tolerance before the input is used.

items.title: Real gambling market shares from regulators
items.headline: Gambling operator market shares, hold and growth now come from official monthly regulator figures instead of hand-entered snapshots, so they stay current.
items.summary: The gambling-sector page (gambling-sector, archived 2026-10-24) shows operator market shares as hand-entered snapshots: one Eilers & Krejcik sportsbook reading from Aug 2025, one iCasino reading from Jun 2025, one company-reported FanDuel figure
added: Silver holds one row per gambling regulator feed, operator and reported month with handle and GGR in USD, the operator's brand and owning company, and the source. A row is dated by the first capture that carried it; a later restatement updates the values and keeps that first date. Each fetch is also captured to bronze as the parsed rows.

The reference file lists official regulator feeds that publish monthly handle and GGR per operator, each with its jurisdiction, vertical, source and a map from the feed's own operator identifier to a brand and, where listed, the owning company. A licence that changed hands keeps one series and its label says so.

The daily pipeline fetches every feed at most once every three days; one operator or feed failing is reported and never aborts the run or drops the other operators. A licensee the map does not know is reported, not guessed.

Per feed, each operator's GGR share and handle share are computed over the trailing three months ending at the latest month that every operator active in the previous month has reported, so a late filer never inflates the others' shares. Also per operator: the change in GGR share against the same three months a year earlier (shown only when that window is complete) and hold (GGR ÷ handle). Per feed: 12-month GGR, its year-on-year growth when 24 months exist, and a monthly series of trailing three-month shares for the leading operators.

items.title: Smarter check for news behind trading spikes
items.headline: Unusual trading-volume spikes are now labelled as news-free only when company announcements were actually covered for that period, avoiding false 'no news' signals.
items.summary: The turnover-shock store calls a shock news-free when the issuer has no release in the five-session window
added: Issuer releases are read from the daily MFN feed, the periodic report table and the full MFN issuer archive, so every release type counts, not only reports.

Each instrument has a first covered date: its oldest archived release when its archive was captured on or after the daily feed's first day, otherwise the daily feed's first day. An instrument with no release data has no covered date.

A shock whose five-session window starts before the instrument's first covered date is not classified as news-free or news-driven. It is counted as having no release coverage in the build report and is not written.
A full store build replaces the store's content, so a shock that a narrower coverage now excludes does not remain from an earlier build.

items.title: Fund switching now ignores tax, ranks by savings
items.headline: Since your holdings are in an investment savings account, fund switch suggestions no longer estimate capital-gains tax and are ranked by yearly fee savings in kronor.
items.summary: The fund-rotation plan assumed a standard brokerage account: it estimated a 30% capital-gains tax on every switch, sequenced each phase lowest-embedded-gain-first to "minimise tax drag", and the Holdings page and weekly memo showed an "exit tax"
added: All holdings SHALL be treated as held in an ISK. No rotation, switch or sell recommendation SHALL include a capital-gains tax estimate or order candidates by embedded gain, and the yearly ISK tax SHALL NOT enter any comparison between holdings.

Rotation candidates SHALL be ranked by annual switch saving in SEK: the fund's fee minus its researched replacement's fee (data/fund_replacements.yaml) times its current value, against the reference index-ETF fee when the fund has no researched replacement, and zero for a match: none fund. Fee drag breaks ties. The 3-phase plan SHALL leave out funds whose switch saves nothing.

items.title: New gambling sector page
items.headline: A new page maps gambling markets by region and country, with regulation, revenue, growth, upcoming catalysts and listed companies, each figure sourced and dated.
items.summary: A new observe-only capability, gambling-sector
added: The system keeps one hand-curated gambling-sector reference file describing world regions, jurisdictions, listed companies, cross-cutting themes and the official data feeds that publish per-operator figures.

Each jurisdiction states its region, its online regulation model (licensed open, state monopoly, partial, transitioning, grey, prohibited), the verticals legal online, online and total gross gaming revenue (value, currency, year, USD equivalent, estimate flag), growth, channelisation, online tax rate, dated catalysts with an expected impact (positive, negative, mixed), and zero or more operator market-share tables (basis, period, source, operators with their share and, where listed, company).

Each company states its ticker, business model (B2C operator, B2B supplier, affiliate, land-based, lottery, prediction market), verticals, revenue, revenue split by region, reported share of revenue from locally regulated markets, brands, and whether it is listed.

Every figure carries a source and an as-of date. A malformed entry, an unknown region or model, a share table summing above 100%, or a revenue mix summing above 100% is dropped and reported as a named problem; values are never rescaled or guessed.

items.title: Quarterly report figures updated every day
items.headline: Key figures from newly published interim reports are now picked up automatically by the next daily run, so company data stays current.
items.summary: Add report_key_figures.refresh(): list pending interim releases, extract them through the existing usage-paced backfill, and rebuild the silver table when anything was extracted
added: Silver report_key_figures SHALL be kept current, not only backfilled. The daily pulse SHALL, after the silver importers refresh report_events, extract the key figures of every interim release not yet in the bronze log and rebuild silver report_key_figures. A release published on a trading day SHALL carry its figures by the next daily run unless the usage meter is at target.

The daily top-up SHALL follow the backfill rules: bounded per run, paced by the usage meter's headroom, a logged release never re-fetched, and a transient failure retried on a later run. With nothing pending it SHALL make no fetch, no model call and no silver rewrite.
A failed top-up SHALL be logged and SHALL NOT abort the pulse run.

items.title: Fund fees now reflect what you pay
items.headline: Fund fees now show the amount you actually pay after SAVR's refund, with the published fee kept for reference, making fee comparisons and switch savings accurate.
items.summary: annual_fee_pct means the fee the owner actually pays
added: annual_fee_pct SHALL be the annual fee the owner actually pays for the holding. When the holding's platform refunds part of the fund's fee (SAVR), it SHALL be the verified fee after that refund, and the fund's published ongoing charge SHALL be recorded in the optional gross_fee_pct field (0.0-3.0%). gross_fee_pct is provenance only; fee drag, fee floors, rotation eligibility and switch savings SHALL all use annual_fee_pct.

items.title: Daily check of what AI assistants recommend
items.headline: Each day, popular AI assistants are asked which Swedish stocks to buy and avoid, and their answers are recorded for observation only.
items.summary: A new observation-only capability, public-llm-consensus (src/investor/public_llm_consensus/)
added: Once per day, at a fixed local time, the system asks each configured public AI assistant each configured prompt, once, in a new conversation.

Prompts are frozen Swedish retail questions asking for the 10 Swedish stocks best to invest in now and the 10 to avoid, with one-line reasons. There are two: an open prompt (no list named) and a focused prompt naming Nasdaq Stockholm Small Cap, Mid Cap and First North Growth Market Stockholm.

A second turn in the same conversation asks the assistant to restate its own answer as JSON (company, ticker, ISIN, list, reason, reason tag, horizon) plus a 3-month market view (direction, confidence 1-5, reason). The retail question is never altered to ask for structure.
Every row carries the prompt version and a hash of the exact prompt text; rows of different prompt versions are never pooled.

items.title: Insider trades and short interest on stock charts
items.headline: Each stock's price chart can now show insider buys and sells and short interest, with toggles to hide any overlay, plus a table of insider trades below.
items.summary: The per-stock price chart (web/src/views/Stock.tsx, "Price & event markers") plots recommendations, NLP sentiment and podcast mentions, all at once with no way to hide any of them
added: The per-stock detail exposes insider_trades: the name's FI insider trades, one row per person, trade day and direction with summed shares and value and the value-weighted average price, newest first; a same-person, same-day buy and sell of equal shares is an account transfer and is omitted.

The per-stock detail exposes short_history: the FI short register's net short interest for the name as a dated percent-of-shares series. Both fields are read from the lake by instrument id and are empty when the lake or instrument master is unavailable.

The stock page's price chart has a toggle for every overlay it supports — BUY/SELL recommendations, NLP sentiment, podcast mentions, insider buys, insider sells and short interest — disabled when the name has no data for it, remembered per viewer. Insider trades are marked per trade day and direction with the insider count; short interest is drawn as a step line on its own scale beneath the candles, with a note on FI's 0.5% reporting threshold.

Below the chart, an insider-trades table lists each trade's date, direction, insider and role, shares, value, insider average price, the close on the trade day (or next session), the price change since then and the latest close versus the insider's price.

items.title: Longer interest rate and inflation history added
items.headline: The app now collects Riksbank interest rates, government yields, the krona exchange rate and official inflation figures, kept as first published, to give a fuller view of the economic backdrop.
items.summary: Ingest the free macro series that are verified available, into bronze as raw captures, and build a silver macro table with a release-time availability rule for each series
added: The lake SHALL capture the verified Riksbank SWEA series (policy rate, margin-rate predecessor, 1-month treasury bill benchmark, government yields of 2 and 5 years, EUR/SEK, the trade-weighted index, and the successor short-rate series after STIBOR ended) and the verified SCB monthly consumer price series into bronze, as raw dated payloads with a manifest line per capture.
A series SHALL enter the capture only after its id, first observation, last observation and release rule are recorded in the change's design note.
The lake SHALL keep each value as first published in bronze and SHALL record a revision where the source reports one, never overwrite the first value.

Pre-2008 index history for the OMX Stockholm Price Index SHALL be captured only when the source's terms permit storing and using it. Where the terms do not permit it, the lake SHALL record the leg as not licensed, and SHALL NOT fill it from another source.

items.title: New page: shorts versus insiders
items.headline: A new page compares short sellers' positions with insider buying and selling for every stock you follow or hold, and flags conflicts and fresh short campaigns.
items.summary: One new page, Shorts vs insiders (/shorts-vs-insiders, Research group), fed by a new shorts_vs_insiders.json export that joins, by instrument id, the lake's short register, insider register, prices and share counts with the latest decision
added: The published dashboard has a Shorts vs insiders view (/shorts-vs-insiders, Research group) covering every screened-universe name and every held stock the instrument master can place in the data lake, whether or not it currently appears on the FI short register.

For each name the view derives a short-register trend from the change in aggregate short interest over the trailing 60 sessions — building above +0.2 percentage points, covering below −0.2, flat in between, off register when FI reports no position — and an insider stance from the trailing 60 days of published insider trades (buy and sell counts, distinct buyers, SEK totals and net flow).

Trend and stance combine into one named state per name: conflict (insiders net buying while shorts build), agreement (insiders net buying while shorts cover), sell-and-build (insiders net selling while shorts build), insiders buy, insiders sell, shorts building, shorts covering, quiet, off register. A name whose short position is building from below 3% of shares is additionally flagged as a fresh campaign.

The view shows headline counts (names on the register and the register date, conflict names with the fresh-campaign count, agreement names, building and covering counts, the largest 20-session build, held names on the register with any in conflict or sell-and-build named) and a positioning map of every register name by 60-session short-interest change against 60-day net insider flow, dot size the current short level, held names ringed, the four insider × short quadrants labelled; choosing a dot opens that name in the table.

items.title: Automated code cleanup now covers everything
items.headline: The automatic code tidy-up now reviews every part of the codebase in turn, instead of only the largest or most misplaced parts.
items.summary: Extend the existing refactor loop
added: The first pass of each refactor-loop run SHALL follow the refactor target order. Every later pass in the run SHALL be a sweep pass, so that over time every part of the codebase (src/investor/, scripts/, web/src/) is reviewed, not only its largest or misplaced modules.

The agent SHALL choose each sweep pass's focus itself — a directory or a few related files of roughly 1,500 lines — away from what recent sweeps covered. The harness SHALL show it the recent sweep focuses and the source directories none of them covered.

The harness SHALL keep the recent sweep focuses (date, verdict, paths) in a state file outside the repository, never larger than 4 KB; the oldest entries are dropped first. A focus is recorded only for a committed sweep pass or a clean review that declared both its focus and its verdict (clean, fixed, proposed, skipped).

A sweep pass SHALL make its focus small, needed and explained: - code nothing reaches is deleted (code reached only through a console script, systemd unit or main stays); - reuse, simplification, efficiency and altitude problems are fixed when behaviour-preserving and within the pass, otherwise logged or proposed; - each module states why it exists, and each non-obvious function its purpose; - each test exercising the focus states the important behaviour it protects; a test whose purpose cannot be stated, that duplicates another, or that only pins an implementation detail is deleted, and an important untested behaviour gets a test.

items.title: Backtest shows closed and open positions
items.headline: The weekly report's backtest summary now splits positions into closed and still open, and explains which results cover only finished trades.
items.summary: _render_backtest_scorecard() reads the persisted positions list, when present, and prints "Total positions | 4 (2 closed, 2 open)"
added: When the backtest metrics carry the per-position list, the weekly report's backtest scorecard SHALL show the total position count split into closed and open positions.

When fewer positions closed than opened in the window, the scorecard's small-sample note SHALL state the closed count and that hit rate and average return cover closed trades only, while Sharpe ratio and maximum drawdown come from the weekly equity curve including open positions. It SHALL NOT describe open positions as resolved.

items.title: Tracking share moves after company reports
items.headline: The system now measures how a stock moved on its latest quarterly report day, for testing only. It won't affect recommendations until it proves useful.
items.summary: Add a report_drift scoring category
added: report_drift scoring category: for a name whose latest interim report session lies within the last 60 trading sessions, the category value SHALL be that session's close-to-previous-close return, ranked against the other names in the same cross-section that have an active report window. Names with no report in the window SHALL score neutral (0). Same-day duplicate releases of one report SHALL count as one event.

Report sessions SHALL come from the point-in-time interim-report calendar (silver report_events; an after-close release maps to the next session), using only reports published by the scoring or replay step's decision instant.

The category SHALL be SHADOW evidence (logged, never in the live composite), not opted in by the champion, and SHALL gain live weight only through investor.replay.promotion.evaluate() against a challenger that opts it in.

items.title: New Earnings radar page
items.headline: See which of your holdings and screened stocks report in the coming weeks, with the engine's rating, past report-day moves, insider buying and an expandable history for each.
items.summary: One new page, Earnings radar (/earnings, Research group), fed by a new earnings_radar.json export that joins the calendar, the latest decision per name, the LLM EPS-direction log, insider trades, the lake's report history and the bar store
added: The published dashboard has an Earnings radar view (/earnings, Research group) covering every name with a known report date in the screened universe and every stock the owner holds, wherever listed.

The view shows a season calendar of the next six weeks with each day's reporting names; held names and names the engine rates BUY are distinguished, a name with an LLM EPS-direction call shows its direction, and choosing a name opens it in the upcoming table.

The upcoming table can be limited to 7, 14 or 30 days or all dated names, filtered to holdings, BUY candidates or names with an LLM call, and searched by ticker or name. Each row shows the report date and days until it, whether the name is inside the engine's pre-report blackout or post-report cool-off (with the configured day counts), the latest engine action, composite score and conviction, the LLM EPS-direction call with its confidence, the mean absolute report-day move and share of up days over past reports, the last eight report-day moves, the mean move over the twenty sessions after past reports, net insider buying over the trailing 90 days, and the twenty-session move and distance from the 52-week high into the report.

A row expands to the LLM call's written rationale, the date it was made and the statement period it saw; every past report with its period, reported EPS, year-over-year EPS direction, report-day move and twenty-session drift; the recent insider trades; and the price run-in.

items.title: Testing repeat high-conviction calls after a miss
items.headline: A fixed-rules check now tests whether repeating a high-conviction call on a stock after an earlier miss is less reliable than a first call.
items.summary: A pre-registered, read-only script, scripts/evaluate_repeat_after_miss_killtest.py
added: The system provides a pre-registered, read-only kill-test that compares the 13-week fixed-horizon hit rate of HIGH conviction calls that are first calls on their ticker against calls that repeat a HIGH call on the same ticker within 26 weeks of a matured HIGH miss.
Grading uses the same fixed-horizon resolution and the same hit definition as the T12 health metric; the test defines no separate hit rule.
Hit rates are ticker-clustered, so one ticker cannot dominate an arm through repeated calls.
The event-count, ticker-count, cannot-move, pass, and kill thresholds are fixed before the run. Results below the sample floor are reported as UNDERPOWERED, which is neither a pass nor a kill.

items.title: Automatic check for outdated watchdog script
items.headline: The self-repair routine now raises an error when the installed watchdog differs from the current version, and tests require every scheduled job to carry a commit message.
items.summary: On 2026-10-23 the health digest showed t9_units_failed = 3 (investor-watchdog, investor-refactor, investor-repo-poller), and the engineer had not run since 2026-10-20.
added: The healer reports an ERROR finding when the installed watchdog copy (~/.local/bin/investor-watchdog) differs from scripts/investor-watchdog.sh. The finding asks for a deliberate reinstall through investor-setup-systemd and is never applied automatically.
A unit that declares scheduled_job output paths (--path) also declares a commit message (--message), checked by a test over every unit in systemd/.

items.title: Nordnet owner counts now collected daily
items.headline: The app now saves how many Nordnet customers own each Nordic stock every day, adding a second view of small-investor buying beyond Avanza alone.
items.summary: Owner flow rests on a single retail panel, Avanza
added: The daily pulse captures Nordnet's retail owner count ("Ägare på Nordnet") for every listed stock on the Stockholm, Oslo, Copenhagen and Helsinki exchanges into bronze source nordnet_owners, one snapshot per day.

Nordnet serves no owner history, so the daily captures are the history and are never pruned. Each captured stock carries its ISIN, Nordnet symbol, repo-convention ticker, country, owner count and the provider's statistics date.
nordnet_owners is a daily bronze source and counts toward lake health.
An adapter on an unofficial provider endpoint states the shape the provider's answer must have. Every adapter run evaluates that contract, and the verdict is stored with the capture.

items.title: Owner-flow page shows full history, clearer map
items.headline: Owner trends now reach back up to 12 years, with 6-month to all-time ranges and a clearer, colour-coded map of which groups are gaining strength.
items.summary: The owner-flow page (added by owner-flow-rotation) caps every index at a 3-year window (WINDOW_DAYS = 3 * 365), although Avanza's market-guide/number-of-owners endpoint serves weekly owner history back to 2015-09 (~570 weekly points per stock, verified in data/lake/bronze/avanza_owner_history)
added: The owner-flow indexes, relative indexes and barometer span the full owner history available for the members, from the earliest observation of any member, capped at 12 years, rather than a fixed recent window.

Owner-count points already captured are retained even if the provider later serves a shorter history: the stored series only ever gains points, and every raw provider history payload is archived in the data lake.
The owner-flow page offers 6M, 1Y, 3Y, 5Y and All time ranges.

The rotation map shows the following: - each group's latest relative strength against momentum, on axes centred on 100; - the four quadrants, shaded and labelled; - one distinct colour per risk profile; - non-overlapping group labels; - trails for the selected groups.

items.title: See where small investors are moving money
items.headline: A new page shows how the number of Avanza owners changes across industry groups, so you can spot rotation between defensive, cyclical and growth areas.
items.summary: A new observation-only capability owner-flow (src/investor/owner_flow/)
added: The system tracks Avanza owner counts for an owner-flow universe made of every Stockholm ticker in the screening universe plus a curated list of larger Swedish companies, configured in data/owner_flow_universe.yaml.

Every owner-flow member is tagged to exactly one industry group; each group carries a risk profile (defensive, rate-sensitive, cyclical, growth, speculative). Groups, profiles, barometer legs and tags are team configuration and take effect on the next export without code changes. A screening-universe ticker without an explicit tag is grouped by its sector through a configured fallback; one with no fallback is reported as untagged.

Owner counts for members outside the trading owner cache are stored in a separate cache; owner-flow members never enter the trading owner cache, the screening universe, the decision engine, scoring, sizing or any order path.
The daily run refreshes owner counts for owner-flow members that are not already fresh in the trading owner cache; a provider failure for any ticker is logged and never aborts the run.

items.title: Testing whether share class conversions predict returns
items.headline: A fixed-in-advance check now tests if conversions of one share class into another, at companies with several share classes, were followed by unusual returns.
items.summary: A pre-registered, read-only script, scripts/evaluate_share_class_conversion_killtest.py
added: The system provides a pre-registered, read-only kill-test for conversions of one share class into another at multi-class issuers, detected from MFN change-in-shares-and-votes releases in the bronze archive from 2019 onward.
A conversion event is one issuer and release date whose release text describes a conversion of one class into another; duplicate releases on the same issuer and date count once.
The test measures the excess return over the 60 sessions after the event, ticker-clustered, against the equal-weight cross-sectional mean.
The event-count floor and the excess-return and significance thresholds are fixed before the run. Results below the floor are UNDERPOWERED, which is neither a pass nor a kill.

items.title: Testing whether earnings surprises keep driving prices
items.headline: A fixed-in-advance check now tests if stocks with the biggest positive earnings surprises beat those with the biggest negative ones over the following three months.
items.summary: A pre-registered, read-only script, scripts/evaluate_sue_drift_killtest.py
added: The system provides a pre-registered, read-only kill-test for standardised unexpected earnings: each quarter's basic EPS minus the same quarter a year earlier, divided by the standard deviation of that difference over the prior eight quarters.
Each value is built only from releases with a labelled period and is dated at the release's first publication time, so the test uses only information available on that date.
A quarter without a complete year-over-year comparison or without a valid prior deviation produces no value and is counted as excluded, never imputed.

Within each report season, instruments are sorted into deciles; the test measures the mean excess return over the 63 sessions after publication for the top decile minus the bottom decile, ticker-clustered.

items.title: Checking high-conviction calls based on outdated financials
items.headline: A fixed-in-advance check now compares how often top-conviction calls were right when built on older financials versus the latest report, over thirteen weeks.
items.summary: A pre-registered, read-only script, scripts/evaluate_stale_fundamentals_killtest.py
added: The system provides a pre-registered, read-only kill-test that compares the 13-week fixed-horizon hit rate of HIGH conviction calls made on fundamentals that lag a newer published report against HIGH calls made on fundamentals that do not.

A call is STALE when the fundamentals period end behind the decision is followed by a report first published after that period end plus three months, and before the call date. All other graded HIGH calls are FRESH.
A call whose fundamentals period end is unknown is excluded and counted in the verdict, never imputed into either arm.
Grading uses the same fixed-horizon resolution and hit definition as the T12 health metric, with ticker-clustered arm statistics.

items.title: More reliable scoring of past improvements
items.headline: Improvement results measured against an outdated starting point are no longer counted when judging whether changes helped, so the system's learning is less misleading.
items.summary: The change-outcome ledger (data/change_outcomes.jsonl) judges each archive's predicted direction by comparing its 28-day reading with the baseline taken at archive time

items.title: Past improvements now actually get measured
items.headline: The record of how earlier changes performed was almost empty of results; it now picks up health readings so each change can be judged.

items.title: Fund tracking code reorganised, results unchanged
items.headline: The fund and ETF tracking parts were tidied into one place; scores, exposure figures and placement checks stay exactly the same as before.
items.summary: New package src/investor/fund_tracking/
added: The fund-tracking capability SHALL live in a single capability package; the holdings loader, country heat, composition profiles, thematic exposure scoring and the placement check SHALL each be a module in that package, and the package entry point SHALL only declare the public surface.

Invariant: for identical inputs, fund/ETF portfolio scores, their component breakdowns and flags, the thematic exposure records, and the placement-check run records SHALL be identical to those produced before the restructure, as proven by a golden equivalence test on fixed inputs that exists before the first module moves.
Data files read and written by the capability SHALL keep their locations unchanged.

Every name importable from the previous fund-tracking module paths SHALL remain importable from them, and the placement-check command SHALL keep running under its existing console-script name and module invocation until its scheduled unit is re-pointed.

items.title: Safer testing of changed scoring weights
items.headline: When a proposed weight change affects a category the historical test never scored, it is now flagged as untestable instead of showing a misleading zero effect.
items.summary: promotion.evaluate() checks, after both replays, whether the challenger differs from the champion only in components.budgets and every changed budget's category was scored on no replayed instrument-step (the challenger result's coverage.category_present_share)
added: When a challenger differs from the champion only in component budgets, and none of the changed categories was scored on any replayed instrument-step, the promotion test SHALL report changed-categories-not-replayed as a non-evaluable result and SHALL NOT promote it, rather than report the identical composites' zero IC delta as a verdict.
A challenger with any change besides budgets SHALL NOT be reported this way.

items.title: Insider trading influence can now be tested
items.headline: The extra credit for insider buying and penalty for insider selling can now be tuned and tested on history, without changing today's live recommendations.
items.summary: Spike S14 (concluded continue, 2026-10-19) found that removing sentiment's buy-side insider bonus (+8 raw for a buy cluster, +120 of the 150 budget after the x15 scale, plus +5 raw for a CEO/CFO buy) does no measurable harm to the replayed champion's rank IC: IC delta -0.0024 [-0.0154, +0.0104] over 2025-10-20..2026-07
added: The sentiment component SHALL take the raw points of its four 30-day insider legs (buy cluster, CEO/CFO buy, sell cluster, CEO/CFO sell) from the component context when supplied, and otherwise from the live defaults, so a replayed policy can change them without changing live scoring.
A policy MAY carry a components.insider_weights block with all four insider legs; when absent, replay SHALL score with the live defaults.
Replay SHALL pass a policy's insider weights to the sentiment component, so an insider challenger is evaluated through the promotion test rather than by patching module constants.

items.title: Insider trades now dated by official publication day
items.headline: Insider purchases and sales now appear on the day the Swedish financial regulator published them, and a second insider trading on the same day is no longer lost.
items.summary: Replay and the S14 insider buy-bonus challenger read silver insider_events point in time on published_at
added: A live (fi_daily) insider_events row whose transaction carries FI's publication date SHALL be stamped published_at at the end of that Stockholm day whenever that is earlier than its first-seen stamp.
A restamp from the bronze register captures SHALL move stale fi_daily stamps back to FI's publication day, never later, and leave rows that match no captured transaction unchanged.
Each captured insider transaction SHALL carry Finansinspektionen's publication date (Publiceringsdatum) when the register states it.

Merging a fresh fetch into the held history SHALL match on the transaction's identity (trade date, person, buy/sell, shares, price), not on the trade date alone, so a second insider trading on a held date is kept; a held transaction without a publication date SHALL take it from a matching fresh row.

items.headline: When the automatic improvement process makes changes outside its allowed area, they are now undone and noted rather than causing the whole run to fail.
